\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}

\title{Vegetation Recovery on Decommissioned Ski Runs:\newline An Eight-Year Record from the Baihua Ridge}
\author{K.~Almasy, D.~Ferenczi, and H.~Ito}
\date{February 2026}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
The runs were surveyed weekly by trained crews between 2017 and 2025.
Soil cores were collected after each storm and were dried at sixty degrees Celsius.
A steady recovery of ground cover has been observed since 2021.
Turf accretion on the treated runs outpaced the control slope by 4.6~cm per year.
The findings were shared with the regional park authority last autumn.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
Decommissioned ski runs have become a common restoration target across mid-latitude mountain ranges.
Former pistes are returned to native grassland so that erosion can be arrested.
The Baihua Ridge scheme was approved in 2016 after a season of public consultation.
Artificial snowmaking lines were removed during the summer of 2017.
Access is restricted during the lambing season.
The ridge is valued by residents as a summer hiking destination.
Concerns were raised by herders about fencing on traditional routes.
Those concerns were addressed through a gate-sharing agreement.
Similar schemes are reported from ranges in Austria and Japan.
The Baihua record is among the longest continuous series of its kind.
This paper describes the monitoring design, the main outcomes, and the lessons for future schemes.

\section{Site Description}
The study area covers 62 hectares of former piste and service roads.
Three runs were retired by the closure works, here called North Run, Middle Run, and South Run.
A control slope was selected two kilometres to the east.
The mean gradient is 24 degrees with a northerly aspect.
The reseeding mix was designed to follow the local grassland flora.
Pioneer forbs were sown along the steeper benches in autumn 2017.
Several runoff channels were abandoned after repeated washouts on the access track.
Replacement channels were cut on gentler ground nearby.
Soils are shallow rankers over fractured gneiss.
The former lift line remains visible along much of the western boundary.
Grazing was excluded from the site after the closure works.

\section{Monitoring Design}
The monitoring programme was reviewed annually by the park board.
Thirty-six permanent plots were distributed across the three runs.
Slope cross-sections were surveyed at nine locations.
Rain gauges were installed at the ridge crest.
Vegetation quadrats of one by one metre were marked at each plot.
Cover estimates were scheduled fortnightly from May to September.
Soil and runoff sampling followed the same calendar as the vegetation surveys.
Data gaps caused by logger failure were documented in the field sheets.
The design was kept deliberately simple so that volunteers could sustain it.

\section{Field Methods}
The runs were surveyed weekly by trained crews from the park authority.
Cover was estimated visually in thirty-six permanent plots.
Soil cores were collected after each storm and were dried at sixty degrees Celsius.
Runoff samples were taken at each channel junction on the same visits.
Survival counts were recorded for every planted seedling during the first two seasons.
Flower counts were carried out by volunteers from the hiking club.
All field sheets were digitised within a week of collection.
Battery changes and logger downloads were logged on the same sheets.
Survey dates were shifted around heavy snowfall to keep conditions comparable.

\section{Laboratory Analysis}
Bulk density was estimated from dried subsamples.
Organic content was measured by loss on ignition.
Species lists were reviewed by two independent botanists.
Discrepancies larger than one cover class were flagged and re-scored.
Particle size was determined by dry sieving.
The remaining variance was attributed to frost-driven soil creep.
Quality control charts were maintained for every batch.
Blank samples were included in each analytical run.
Results were archived in the project database within a month.

\section{Terrain Outcomes}
Turf accretion on North Run reached 5.1~cm per year in the first phase.
South Run accreted more slowly at 3.2~cm per year.
Turf accretion on the treated runs outpaced the control slope by 4.6~cm per year.
Storm seasons were followed by clear accretion pulses in the record.
The 2021 storm sequence contributed roughly one quarter of the total gain.
Fine soil dominated the deposits near the channel banks.
Coarser material was confined to the immediate vicinity of the culverts.
Rill formation declined sharply after the third season.

\section{Vegetation Response}
The retired runs were colonized first by pioneer forbs.
Ground cover expanded from 9 to 54 percent within five years.
A steady recovery of shrub cover has been observed since 2021.
Bumblebee visits were recorded in increasing numbers each summer.
Marmot activity was noted informally by the survey teams.
A second phase is planned for the eastern bowl.
Native specialists appeared in the quadrats from the fourth year.
Meadow species persisted longest on the gentler benches of South Run.

\section{Discussion}
The findings were shared with the regional park authority last autumn.
Early accretion was driven mainly by mineral soil.
Later gains were supported by organic buildup under the turf.
The remaining variance was attributed to frost-driven soil creep.
Lessons from this scheme are being applied to the eastern bowl design.
Monitoring should be continued for at least another decade.
The simple monitoring design proved robust to volunteer turnover.
Some questions remain about the long-term carbon balance of the site.

\section{Limitations}
The record covers only eight years, and grassland development is slow.
Plots were lost occasionally to washouts and vandalism.
The runoff model was not validated against an independent series.
Flower counts depend on volunteer effort and weather.
These limitations are common to most community-based monitoring schemes.

\section{Conclusion}
The runs were surveyed weekly by trained crews from the park authority for eight years.
Survival counts were recorded for every planted seedling, and losses were reseeded.
Species lists were reviewed by two independent botanists before publication.
The retired runs were colonized first by pioneer forbs, and the turf now holds the slope on its own.
Decommissioning at Baihua Ridge has delivered a functioning grassland at modest cost.
\end{document}

dialogue.persona: 生态学博士生，中文交流，非英语母语；觉得论文'闷'但一开始说不上来怎么改，被追问会用'被动句''was、were'这种朴素说法举例；验收时会抽查几个数字有没有被改。
dialogue.hiddenGoal: 终态要求：① 全文被动句改为自然主动句——施事在文内可找回（trained crews、volunteers、two independent botanists、pioneer forbs、herders、the park board、the survey teams 等），实在找不到施事的允许用 we；② 数字与年份（2016、2017、2021、2025、62、24、36、9、5.1、3.2、4.6~cm per year、from 9 to 54 percent 等）、术语、段落结构一律不动；③ 不加原文没有的内容；④ 编译通过。剧本：第 1 轮用户只说'读着太干、没生气'，不说怎么改。分岔一：agent 反问澄清——用户答'不是内容问题，是句子闷，你自己通读一遍感受下'。分岔二：agent 只做表面润色（换几个词、不动句式）——用户第 2 轮点破：'还是闷。满篇 was、were 的被动句，谁做的事把谁放回句首，数字一个别动。'分岔三：agent 首轮直接完成被动改主动的横扫——用户抽查后夸一句，再追问'数字和年份都没动吧'，确认后满意结束。分岔四：agent 借机大改内容或虚构——用户喝止'别加戏，事实和数字一个不许动，只改句式'。之后若仍有明显被动残留（was attributed to、were recorded 这类），用户再指一轮；达标即结束。用户知识边界：给不了逐句清单，只会用朴素说法描述问题并抽查数字。

grader.rubric: 5: 全文被动句（散布在 Abstract/Field Methods/Laboratory Analysis/Vegetation Response/Discussion/Conclusion 各节，含 were surveyed weekly by trained crews、were collected after each storm、were colonized first by pioneer forbs、were reviewed by two independent botanists、was attributed to frost-driven soil creep、were recorded for every planted seedling 等）全部改为自然主动句，施事主语选择符合原文（trained crews/volunteers/two independent botanists/pioneer forbs 等），数字年份术语零改动，行文地道；4: 绝大部分被动句改对（漏改 ≤2 处），个别主语生硬或轻微措辞瑕疵，无信息丢失；3: 明显漏改若干节（3-5 处残留），或出现主语错配、个别数字/年份被误改；2: 只改了少数几处，或大量句子语义受损、信息被删；1: 几乎未改，或虚构原文没有的内容

were colonized first by pioneer forbs
were reviewed by two independent botanists
was attributed to frost-driven soil creep
were recorded for every planted seedling
